key_insight: Short 2D motion tracklets transfer better than depth-lifted 3D tracklets for estimating deformable-object materials from real drop videos, reversing their ranking in simulation.
engineering_relevance: A single drop video can support rapid estimation of density-normalized stiffness and, when plastic deformation occurs, density-normalized yield stress.
method: Train the feed-forward PhysReader predictor entirely in simulation.
Combine video with short 2D optical-flow tracklets.
Learn a 3D representation by matching a teacher with access to exact 3D deformation.
evidence_signal: On PhysReader-Real—16 everyday objects with five drops each and jointly fitted reference materials checked against tensile tests—PhysReader outperformed all compared inputs and baselines except an optimizer initialized from its predictions, which took 49 minutes per video versus 12 seconds.
watch_item: Synthetic validation can misrank real-world performance; even accurate depth did not resolve the transfer failure of depth-lifted 3D tracklets.
paper_title: What a Drop Reveals: Sim-to-Real Material Estimation for Deformable Objects from Video
